messages.text: For a AI use case involving AI data centers, where would Signaling / Non-signaling Tester fit in the test workflow?

Short answer: In an AI data center use case, Signaling / Non-signaling Tester fits in the **Connectivity test workflow**, alongside other data-center connectivity validation for electrical interconnect, optical interconnect, and fiber deployment; it is not positioned by the passages as a power/cooling/PCB material tester.[5][22]
| Workflow point | Tester role | What it validates in AI data center communications/connectivity context | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Connectivity / communications validation | **Signaling tester / callbox** | Used when the DUT needs an active communications connection: the CMX500 Callbox is positioned to quickly establish a DUT connection and run RF, mobility, application, NTN, WLAN/cellular desense, pre-conformance, and related R&D verification.[9] | [9] |
| R&D and pre-conformance phase | **Signaling tester / callbox** | Fits before formal certification or deployment-style validation, because the CMX500 use cases include R&D verification, sensitivity testing, 3GPP pre-conformance testing, high end-to-end throughput testing, and other RF/application-oriented checks.[1][9] | [1][9] |
| RF verification without full protocol session | **Non-signaling tester / non-signaling mode** | Fits as a non-signaling verification step in R&D, where the knowledge base explicitly lists “Non-signaling verification” as a CMX500 Callbox use case.[1] | [1] |
| AI data center connectivity coverage boundary | **Not the whole data-center test stack** | AI/data-center connectivity also includes high-speed electrical interconnect, optical interconnect, fiber deployment, rack power distribution, busbar, cooling, and leak detection, so Signaling / Non-signaling Tester only covers the communications/connectivity portion, not all infrastructure tests.[5] | [5] |
【推論】For an AI data center project, place the Signaling / Non-signaling Tester after component-level interconnect planning and before deployment/system validation, specifically where a communications DUT or connectivity subsystem must be connected, characterized, or pre-conformance checked; this inference combines the AI data center “Connectivity” focus with the CMX500’s DUT-connection, RF, application, desense, pre-conformance, and non-signaling verification roles.[5][9][1][22]
